text:
liz: Quick heads-up — AWS Marketplace and a couple hardware partners flagged that packaged SDK wheels need explicit platform tags for arm64 mac builds and linux-gpu CUDA builds. They won't accept a single 'universal' wheel for marketplace listing. This affects our next SDK release and could break partner install flows if we don't coordinate.

kevin: What specifically will break for partners? Is it just pip install failing or runtime CUDA mismatches?

olga: Two things: marketplace requires separate wheels per ABI/platform, and our current build produces a single manylinux wheel with a post-install binary blob assuming x86_64 CUDA. For arm64 mac & linux-gpu we need distinct wheels because of native binaries / CUDA libs. That means the filenames/tags will change, and older environment installers will not auto-resolve a correctly built wheel.

ashish: From HW partner side (NVIDIA SI) this mainly shows up as import errors like: ImportError: libcudart.so.11: cannot open shared object file. They want a test matrix so they can validate their AMIs/VM images. Timeline?

liz: I propose a coordination plan: 1) we introduce a compatibility shim package 'redwood-inference-compat' that maps old top-level imports to the new runtime package, 2) release SDK with new wheels (major semver bump because ABI changes), 3) run partner canaries (marketplace test account + 3 HW partners), 4) docs + partner communication + 8-week deprecation window for old wheel resolution.

kevin: +1 on the shim. Can we make the shim tiny so it never pulls the wrong binary? Like it should detect platform and raise a clear error instructing to pip install the correct wheel.

olga: Exactly. Example shim (very small):

```
# redwood_inference/__init__.py (compat shim)
import platform, sys
arch = platform.machine()
if arch == 'x86_64' and 'cuda' in sys.modules: # pseudo-check
    from redwood_runtime_x86 import *
elif arch == 'arm64':
    raise RuntimeError('Arm64 wheel required. pip install redwood-runtime-arm64')
else:
    raise RuntimeError('Platform not supported. See https://redwood.ai/sdk/platform-wheels')
```

olga: The point is to fail fast with actionable instruction. We shouldn't silently fallback to a CPU-only wheel for GPU workloads.

ashish: For partner validation we need a matrix: ubuntu20+cuda11, ubuntu22+cuda12, macos-arm64 (no CUDA), windows-cuda. I can coordinate NVIDIA and the two SI partners to run smoke tests. Prefer a 2-week partner validation window.

kevin: For release process, propose: branch cut -> build and upload staged wheels to internal index -> canary partners install from that index -> we collect logs -> flip marketplace listing to the new artifacts. Which CI jobs need updates? windows-wheel, linux-cuda-build, mac-arm-build. I'm tagging olga to modify the build matrix.

deploy-bot: CI failure in windows-wheel at 2223334522: build/test/wheels/windows-wheel failed on packaging step. link: https://ci.redwood.ai/2223334522

olga: saw that, investigating. It's unrelated (MSVC linker flag for our custom CUDA shim). I'll patch the build to isolate the shim so the wheel metadata is still correct while linker issues are fixed.

liz: Messaging: we should send partners a one-pager + sample pip commands and an example of how to detect wrong wheel at runtime. Also provide marketplace listing FAQ for partners. Draft timeline: week 0: announce, week 1: build & staged wheels, week 2-3: partner canaries, week 4: public marketplace cutover, week 12: old wheel resolution removed. Thoughts?

ashish: Works for us. Can we get early access to staged wheels by Friday? I'll sync SI timelines.

kevin: I'll add a failing-but-helpful error in the shim so if someone hits it during canary we capture clear telemetry. Also bump major version in setup.cfg and add a 'migration.md' in the SDK repo.

olga: Action items: 1) olga — update CI matrix and add arm64/mac wheel job (due Thu), 2) kevin — add clear runtime error + telemetry hooks (due Fri), 3) liz — draft partner one-pager + marketplace FAQ (due Wed), 4) ashish — schedule SI/NVIDIA canary runs and provide test AMIs (due Fri). I'll update the staged-index and post the pip install commands when builds are ready.

liz: Thanks all. I'll @partners in the partner channel once we have the staged index URL.

kevin: +1, and please tag support and eng-oncall if canaries show import errors we can't reproduce internally.

olga: Putting a temporary note in the SDK README about the breaking ABI change and example resolution commands: `pip install --index-url https://staged-artifacts.redwood.ai redwood-runtime-x86==2.0.0`

liz: Closing this thread when the staged URL is posted. For now, marking as coordinated plan and actionable owners. :thumbsup:
